title: Source-cell presentation for the operadic outer-horn problem
statement:
Use the families, fiberwise inert arrows, active arrows and incidence diagrams of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence], small simplicial sets and standard horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and categorical equivalences and cofibrations of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $n\geq1$ and $\pi:\mathcal P\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ be a small family with space zero-fibers and with every parameter-edge correspondence constant over $[0]$. Require the inert lifts over $(\alpha,\operatorname{id}_t)$ to be $\pi$-cocartesian in the whole family, not only cocartesian after restriction to a parameter fiber; these are the stationary inert lifts used below. Write $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_0$, $\mathcal P^-=\mathcal P\times_{\Delta^n}\Lambda_0^n$, and $\mathcal P^+=\mathcal P\times_{\Delta^n}\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$.

The inclusion $\mathcal P^-\hookrightarrow\mathcal P$ has an exhaustive well-ordered relative cell presentation over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ of the following form. There are simplicial subsets starting at $\mathcal P^-$, with union $\mathcal P$, and each successor is obtained by a pushout of an attaching map described below followed by a monomorphism which is a categorical equivalence; at limit stages take unions. An attaching diagram can first be replaced relative to its boundary by a diagram whose comparison to it is a categorical trivial cofibration. The permitted attaching diagrams are:

(a) $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\hookrightarrow X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ for a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P^+$ all of whose arrows are active and whose final vertex is a color. Here $X_\sigma=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/\sigma}$ is the join slice: its $k$-simplices extend $\sigma$ to $\Delta^k\star\Delta^d$ with first factor in $\mathcal A$. The attaching map evaluates this join diagram in $\mathcal P$.

(b) $X_\sigma\star\partial\Delta^d\hookrightarrow X_\sigma\star\Delta^d$ with final vertex of $\sigma$ over $[0]$.

(c) $\partial\Delta^d\star L_\tau\hookrightarrow\Delta^d\star L_\tau$, where $\tau:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P$ ends over $([r],t)$ with $t>0$. The simplex $\tau$ is taken in the whole family: it may have an initial block of any number of vertices in $\mathcal A$, followed by a nonempty block in $\mathcal P^+$. Its arrows, including those across the parameter change, need not be active. The displayed cell adjoins $\tau$ itself as well as its inert incidence extension; the face $\tau$ need not already be in the previous subset. Here $L_\tau$ is the following simplicial subset of the join undercategory $\mathcal P_{\tau/}$. Its $k$-simplices are maps $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to\mathcal P$ equal to $\tau$ on the first factor, with the last factor in the parameter fiber $t$ of $\tau(d)$, every vertex of the last factor over $[0]$ or $[1]$, and every base edge from $\tau(d)$ to that factor, and within that factor, inert. Its operators restrict the last factor. These are all arrows over inert base maps, not just cocartesian arrows. Thus $L_\tau$ retains the noninvertible morphisms between possible inert extensions; it is a quasicategory, not the ordinary category of simplices of that quasicategory. Let $I_r$ have the $r$ edge objects $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, the $r+1$ vertex objects $v_0,\ldots,v_r$, and arrows $e_j\to v_{j-1},v_j$ only, besides identities. Chosen fiberwise cocartesian inert lifts give a distinguished diagram $i:N(I_r)\to L_\tau$. For a simplicial map $g:T\to E$, define the left join-cone simplicial set $E_{/g}$ by $(E_{/g})_a=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^a\star T,E)$ with restriction to $T$ equal to $g$; its operators are induced by the simplex factor. For any inner fibration $q:E\to D$ of quasicategories and any diagram $f:L_\tau\to E$, restriction on left join-cone categories is a trivial Kan fibration:
$$E_{/f}\longrightarrow E_{/fi}\times_{D_{/qfi}}D_{/qf}.$$
Here an $a$-simplex of $E_{/f}$ is a map $\Delta^a\star L_\tau\to E$ restricting to $f$ on the last factor. Thus a lift of a simplex of cones on the distinguished incidence diagram extends to the full inert-extension diagram with any already prescribed boundary and base. This is a cone-restriction assertion, not a categorical equivalence $N(I_r)\simeq L_\tau$. For $d=0$ this adjoins the object over $[r]$ and its inert projections after their incidence diagram has been adjoined. For $d>0$ the cone at the final vertex of $\partial\Delta^d$ is already present, even when some earlier vertices of $\tau$ are in $\mathcal A$. In particular, for an edge $a\to b$ from $\mathcal A$ to a tuple, the domain is $\{a,b\}\star L_\tau$ and the codomain is $\Delta^1\star L_\tau$; the edge $a\to b$ is a new face of this codomain. There is no requirement that it factor through a color.

The order has these properties. It is first organized by the dimension of the image of the nonempty positive-parameter tail in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$, with faces and their inert associates ordered so that every attaching boundary is already present. Within a fixed tail stage the type-(c) cells run through the whole simplices $\tau$ above, in increasing dimension, including all their initial $\mathcal A$ blocks; limits are taken before advancing to the next tail stage. A type-(c) cell at a vertex and its chosen inert incidence legs precedes the positive-dimensional type-(c) cells ending at that vertex. For $n=1$, the zero-tail stage first adjoins the source cones at colors by type (a), the zero-output source cones by type (b), and then the type-(c) cells with arbitrary $\mathcal A$ prefix and tail image a tuple vertex. Consequently the entire source cone at every tuple, including its mixed simplices and their composites with inert projections, is present before any type-(a) cell whose first vertex is that tuple and whose base image has positive dimension. Type-(a) cells with a color first vertex use its earlier source cone. For $n>1$, a new type-(a) simplex begins at parameter $1$, so its source cone is in $\mathcal P^-$; positive-dimensional type-(c) cells still include the initial $\mathcal A$ blocks not in that horn. More generally every type-(a) cell of positive dimension has its whole first-vertex source cone and its inert projections already present. Every stationary inert edge into a color occurs among the distinguished inert legs, or is identified with such a leg by an equivalence over the same inert base map. All simplices with an $\mathcal A$ prefix and non-color positive tail are covered by the type-(c) cells and the explicitly stated categorical-equivalence comparisons. The filtration is constructed from the source family alone; its local cone-restriction comparison supplies no functor from $\mathcal P$ into a target and assumes no colimits in a target.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.5 and the source-domain filtration in the proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed pp. 332–341, steps (1), (2), (3). For the nonsymmetric generalized version in GH Theorem A.3.4, strongly inert means inert with stationary parameter; the incidence diagram includes both edges and endpoints. This is the domain presentation and its local inert cone-restriction comparison, not the target extension theorem; the restriction on p. 341 is a trivial Kan fibration because the chosen projection diagram is left anodyne in the full inert-extension category. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact. Repair: the simplices tau_b in step (3), printed p. 340, are simplices of the whole M, not just of its positive-parameter restriction. Their positive tails cover the open base simplex. This is essential for the mixed source-to-tuple faces. The order is the F(m) filtration (p. 335) with the associate ordering (pp. 338–340), followed by increasing dimension of the full tau_b. Stationary inert lifts are globally pi-cocartesian, as in HA Definition 2.3.2.10(a), printed p. 253, and GH A.3.1(1).
